To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the early work‐life trajectories of young men and women are becoming more similar, but remain highly gendered.

(1) there is a strong relationship between the occupational structure of the labour market and the pattern of transitions; (2) the occupational structure of labour market has changed substantially in recent decades; (3) these changes have led to substantial changes in the patterns of transition; and (4) these changes have had a significant impact on the early careers of young people.

the occupational structure of the economy has changed over the past 50 years with an increase in the proportion of people in non‐manual jobs; there has been an increase in early work‐life transitions for both women and men, with a decrease in the proportion of women who remain in the same occupation as they had when they first entered the labour market; and, there has been an increasing gender convergence in early work‐ life mobility patterns.

the changing patterns of transition to work and subsequent mobility in the labour market over the twentieth century.
the ways in which the labour market experience and early life trajectories of young people have been shaped by the changing nature of work and the occupational structure.

the ways in which the labour market experiences of young people have changed over time, with particular reference to changes in the occupational structures and the associated changes in the ways in which young people enter work.
